detail: ticket 2: first merge passed, 0 merge failure(s), 14 steps; recall showed 4 fact(s)

memories_after: [Fact w=1.00] (ticket:AGN-2 {"project":"docs"}) The docs project's deliverables/hello.txt follows the owning-team format: line 1 'Owner: docs-team', line 2 'hello', saved as UTF-8 without a BOM.

[Fact w=1.00] (ticket:AGN-2 {"language":"powershell","os":"windows"}) On Windows PowerShell, write files without a UTF-8 BOM using [IO.File]::WriteAllText with New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding($false), so the first line stays byte-exact (starts with 'O', not 239,187,191).
[Fact w=1.00] (ticket:AGN-2 {"project":"docs"}) The docs project's agenium.toml sets key_prefix = "AGN", main_branch = "main", template = "coding@1", and an empty pre_merge check.

[Fact untrusted w=1.00] (ticket:AGN-1 {}) Agenium's write_file tool refuses to overwrite an existing file that has not been read in the session (read_first error), so read_file the target before writing.

[Lesson w=1.00] (ticket:AGN-1 {"project":"docs"}) When writing any file into deliverables/ or reports/ in the docs project, put the owning-team line first (e.g. line 1 'Owner: docs-team') with the requested content lines after it, and save without a UTF-8 BOM so the first line is byte-exact; this makes the pre-merge check pass.

[Lesson w=1.00] (ticket:AGN-1 {"project":"docs"}) The docs project pre-merge check enforces the owning-team first line even when the ticket's acceptance criteria only describe content, so a deliverables/ or reports/ file whose first line is not exactly 'Owner: docs-team' fails the merge and the ticket is reopened.
[Fact w=1.00] (ticket:AGN-1 {"project":"docs"}) The docs project keeps team documents in deliverables/ and reports/, with README.md and agenium.toml at the repo root.
[Fact w=1.00] (ticket:AGN-1 {"project":"docs"}) In the docs project, every team document placed in deliverables/ or reports/ must name its owning team on its first line, e.g. 'Owner: docs-team'.
